key_highlights: ASX on track for fourth consecutive losing week; banks and miners leading declines after shaky Wall Street session
RBA signals continued rate hikes despite surging unemployment — 'interest rate pincer' squeezing households
Australian house prices over halfway to largest 40-year decline; Victoria worst-hit state
AUD weakness accelerating ('trapdoor opens') amid global risk-off and US policy uncertainty
Intergenerational Report 2026 flags urgent need for tax reform amid fiscal deterioration
Gold exploration sector active: Aurum (155g/t), Zenith (6/6 hits WA), Auric (Munda), Aureka (VIC) reporting strong results
Jetstar industrial action escalates; Star casino licence remains suspended — pressure on consumer/leisure names
Data centre energy demand creating structural tension for Australian power grid and energy sector

sectors.trend: Large-cap miners (BHP, RIO, FMG) under pressure from Wall Street spillover and AUD weakness; however, gold exploration small-caps showing strong assay results (Aurum, Zenith, Auric, Aureka, Sarytogan copper). Rio2 Peruvian copper drill and Vista Gold sale signal M&A activity.
sectors.implications: Gold miners and explorers benefit from safe-haven flows amid rate uncertainty; iron ore/coal names face headwinds from China policy ambiguity and global risk-off. Small-cap gold names offer relative outperformance.

sectors.trend: Big Four banks (CBA, ANZ, NAB, WBC) weighing on ASX; RBA hawkish bias despite unemployment surge creates margin pressure and credit risk concerns. Intergenerational Report 2026 highlights fiscal stress.
sectors.implications: NIMs may compress as RBA hikes outpace deposit pricing; credit losses could rise with renter distress (57% struggling). Defensive dividend yield remains attractive but capital preservation at risk.

sectors.trend: Data centre boom creating energy demand surge but grid constraints ('energy bust'); structural tension between digital infrastructure growth and power supply adequacy.
sectors.implications: Energy generators (AGL, GPG, CGP) face demand tailwinds but capex pressure; renewable developers benefit from policy support. Watch for regulatory intervention on data centre siting.

sectors.trend: Jetstar industrial action (fee waivers), Star casino licence suspended, Ozempic impact on food demand (McDonald's), Coke innovation race — consumer spending under multi-front pressure.
sectors.implications: Qantas (QAN), WES, WOW, and leisure names face margin compression. Consumer staples (WOW, WES) offer relative defensibility but volume growth is challenged.

sectors.trend: House prices over halfway to 40-year decline; Victorian CBD tower listed at $40m; Dusty Martin selling $20m portfolio. Renter distress at 50%+ signals demand softening.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW, DGL, ICV) face occupancy and valuation pressure. Residential construction names (WTC, MTD) may see delayed demand. Commercial REITs under pressure from rate environment.

sectors.trend: OpenAI Medicare data breach raises cybersecurity and data governance concerns; vaccine clinic opens for measles outbreak; AI adoption in small business and workplace accelerating.
sectors.implications: CSL, SGH, and healthcare IT names benefit from data security demand. AI infrastructure plays (ASX-listed) see interest but execution risk remains. Measles outbreak supports CSL vaccine pipeline.

key_themes: RBA rate pincer: hiking into rising unemployment creates household squeeze and credit risk
AUD structural weakness: 'trapdoor' dynamics from US policy uncertainty and China geopolitical risk
Property correction: largest 40-year decline underway, concentrated in Victoria
Gold exploration renaissance: multiple ASX small-caps reporting high-grade results
Fiscal sustainability: Intergenerational Report 2026 demands tax reform
Energy transition tension: data centre demand vs grid capacity
Consumer stress: renter affordability, industrial action, health product disruption

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA hiking into recession / credit cycle deterioration
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce financials exposure; favour quality dividend payers with low gearing; monitor NAB/CBA credit loss provisions

risk_assessment.risk_factor: AUD sustained depreciation and capital outflows
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge AUD exposure; favour export-oriented miners (BHP, RIO) that benefit from weaker AUD; avoid import-dependent consumer names
Underweight residential REITs and construction; monitor Victorian housing data; favour industrial/infrastructure REITs
Diversify away from China-revenue-dependent miners; hold gold as hedge; monitor iron ore contract pricing
Monitor QAN, airline and transport names; assess Jetstar fee waiver impact on Qantas margins

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fiscal deterioration and tax reform uncertainty
risk_assessment.mitigation: Prepare for potential capital gains or dividend tax changes; favour cash-rich balance sheets

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold exploration and production names amid safe-haven flows and AUD weakness
opportunities.rationale: Multiple high-grade assay results (Aurum 155g/t, Zenith 6/6, Auric Munda) signal sector-wide upside; AUD depreciation boosts AUD-denominated gold revenue

opportunities.recommendation: Favour large-cap diversified miners with AUD-weakness hedge
opportunities.rationale: BHP and RIO benefit from weaker AUD on USD-priced commodities; gold and copper exposure provides diversification vs iron ore cyclicality

opportunities.recommendation: Selective energy/infrastructure exposure for data centre demand
opportunities.rationale: Structural power demand from data centres supports generators and grid infrastructure; policy tailwinds for renewables

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to residential REITs and Victorian property-linked names
defensive_moves.rationale: 40-year house price decline underway; renter distress at 50%+ signals demand deterioration; rate pincer worsens affordability

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim consumer discretionary and leisure exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Jetstar industrial action, Star casino suspension, Ozempic demand shift, and renter stress compress consumer spending

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash or short-duration bonds as portfolio ballast
defensive_moves.rationale: Fourth consecutive losing week; bond-yield volatility ('will bonds crash stocks'); RBA hiking cycle not yet complete

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. Fourth consecutive losing week likely to continue as RBA hawkish bias, AUD weakness, and property decline dominate. Banks and miners under pressure from Wall Street spillover. Expect volatility around RBA communications and US policy headlines. ASX 200 likely testing key support levels.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive on quality. Gold miners, diversified resources, and energy infrastructure offer structural tailwinds. Property correction may create entry points in 6-12 months. Tax reform (Intergenerational Report) could reshape equity valuations. AI adoption in Australian business provides medium-term productivity uplift.
